steps.what: Assist anesthesiologists in monitoring patient physiology and responding to changes

tasks.design: Keep active patient observation, interpretation and escalation with the anesthesia team. The {OTHER} physiological monitoring system already produces readings; its runtime is not removable human work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patient safety depends on continuous attention and immediate contextual response.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing monitoring equipment supports care without establishing less human monitoring time.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing artefact from deterioration and coordinating rapid action.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the whole patient and communicate urgent changes.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring responsibility and attention time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Use agreed escalation signals and clinical context

evidence.claim: Existing physiological data capture does not itself remove clinical monitoring effort; no relevant validated labour saving is supplied in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant monitoring support, excluding anesthesiologist time and unrelated procedures. Concurrent monitoring is allocated once in roll-ups.
Monitoring equipment and laboratory processes produce readings under existing workflows; assistant interpretation and artefact checks retain all time. No new autonomous response is assumed.
Use existing native monitor configuration first. No changed process adds incremental upkeep; national rules and local delegation govern care scope.
research_questions: Which monitoring actions require continuous bedside attention despite automatic readings?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Automatic measurement already exists; bedside attention, interpretation and response retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collect and clarify patients' pre-anesthetic health histories
Document and confirm the pre-anesthetic history for clinical review

loop.purpose: Draft a faithful pre-anesthetic history record
loop.input: Consented interview account or assistant dictation plus relevant prior record
loop.output: Draft history with conflicts and missing answers marked
loop.check: Assistant checks previous anesthesia reactions, allergies, medicines, conditions, timing, negation and source attribution against the original account
loop.stop: One draft; missing or conflicting facts require direct clarification and manual documentation
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative answers and contradictions require contextual wording beyond copying fields

tasks.design: Draft history wording in the {OTHER} clinical record system from the interview or assistant dictation. The assistant verifies the exact history before confirmation for anesthesiologist review; the tool does not decide fitness for anesthesia.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative history must be recorded accurately after clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical note drafting with clinician validation exists; pre-anesthetic transfer needs local evaluation.
tasks.still_hard: Missed reactions, ambiguous medicines and contradictory accounts.
tasks.human_edge: Ask focused follow-up questions and recognise concerning history.
tasks.altitude: Less initial wording with unchanged history-taking and clinical review boundaries.

reach.learn: Present uncertainty without turning it into an unsupported conclusion

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation records that clinicians validate; this supports the documentation pattern rather than a validated pre-anesthetic assessment.
A 30% reduction in the documentation component is an unmeasured scenario with history collection retained.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant history collection and recording, excluding anesthesiologist risk assessment and anesthesia decisions.

Assistant produces reactions, allergies, medicines, conditions, chronology and source attribution in s1. Its full 65 hours include interview capture and clarification; no structured risk flags are assumed.
Test native forms and dictation first. Without permitted recording use counted dictation or manual notes; the assistant must resolve uncertain content.
Three additional focal hours cover source audits, templates and failed drafts; existing anesthesiologist review is unchanged.
research_questions: Does draft documentation save time after source checks without missing relevant anesthesia history?

already_counted.description: History source checking, correction and confirmation

incremental.description: Source audits, template maintenance and exceptional failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact history record, patient identity, date, sources and unresolved uncertainties; any edit requires renewed confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65+24.5=89.5, gross=10.5, upkeep=3, net=7.5. High assumes 30% less documentation effort with complete source accounts; low retains manual documentation for conflicting or incomplete histories plus upkeep. Interview and anesthesiologist review never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Verify operating room supplies, medicines and gases

steps.what: Verify availability of operating room supplies, medications and gases

tasks.design: Retain direct readiness verification of supplies, medicines and gases. Existing {DOCS} checklists support the check; a stock balance alone does not establish usable items and functioning supply at the point of care.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual readiness can differ from nominal inventory.
tasks.enabler_now: No relevant validated replacement for this readiness check is supplied in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising missing, unsuitable or unavailable items before care starts.
tasks.human_edge: Check physical readiness and escalate concerns immediately.
tasks.altitude: Readiness-check time and responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Inventory records do not alone prove point-of-care supply readiness; this design retains direct verification.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant availability verification, excluding procurement, pharmacy preparation and repairs.
Assistant produces readiness observations in the fully counted step. No structured stock or gas status feed is assumed to replace the physical check.
Use existing checklists first. Unchanged readiness verification has zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Division of pharmacy and technical responsibilities
research_questions: Which readiness failures would remain invisible in nominal stock records?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Physical readiness verification retains all effort; no inventory runtime is counted as labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor patients' progress during the post-anesthesia period
Document verified post-anesthesia observations and actions

tasks.design: Retain recovery observation and verified documentation in the {OTHER} clinical monitoring and record system. Existing automatic readings are not treated as new savings, and the digest does not validate automated recovery narratives or clinical decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recovery assessment combines measured values, behaviour and care actions.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional validated capability is assumed beyond existing monitoring and records.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising deterioration and documenting actions accurately during care.
tasks.human_edge: Observe clinical recovery and communicate important changes.
tasks.altitude: Recovery monitoring and documentation responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Agree the observations and actions needed for safe continuity

evidence.claim: Generic consultation-note drafting does not establish a validated saving for live post-anesthesia monitoring and recovery documentation.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant post-anesthesia care and documentation, distinct from intraoperative monitoring. Concurrent care and charting time must be allocated once in roll-ups.

Assistant produces recovery observations and action records during counted care; monitoring equipment supplies readings through existing processes. No free structured clinical interpretation is assumed.
Test native record features before considering new integration. Existing automatic capture earns no additional human saving.
No new tool or process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero; national rules and local supervision remain applicable.
research_questions: Which recording effort remains after native automatic measurement capture?

incremental.description: No changed recovery monitoring or recording system

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80+20=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Live observation and verified recovery records retain full effort; pre-existing equipment capture is not claimed as a new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Some pre-anesthetic history wording may take less time; patient monitoring, readiness checks and recovery care remain fully staffed professional work.
reach: Align recovery handover with registered nurses
skills_to_grow: Measuring documentation effort separately from care attention
role.ambitious_version: An anesthesia assistant with traceable pre-anesthetic histories who retains direct attention to patient condition and operating-room readiness.
